## System Preferences Dialog Overview
WindMil allows you to set system preferences to customize how the program behaves. These preferences control things like file paths, units of measurement, and default construction types
system:
## Location of User-Defined Templates 
Displays the path where WindMil will look for user-defined databox templates. WindMil will only be able to find user-defined templates in this directory. 

## Default User-Defined Data Template 
Defines the default template file to be used for user-defined data boxes. 

## Display Units 
Provides options for length based on the unit of measurement selected. The WindMil dialog boxes, reports, and status bar will reflect the appropriate lengths. 

## Save Calculated Data 
Causes calculated voltage currents and fault currents to be saved to the disk when you save the model. This means that this analysis data will be available after you close and reopen a model. If this option is not selected, only base or required data will be saved, which means your circuit model will save more quickly and take less space on disk. 

## Left Mouse Button Zoom 
Allows you to zoom in to a region by left-clicking and dragging a rectangle around the region. If this option is not selected, the left-click drag combination selects any elements inside the rectangle. You can still zoom into a region by holding down the right mouse button and performing a left-click drag. 

## Use Auto Panning 
Displays helpful zoom levels. If you click on an element that is partly off-screen, WindMil will automatically shift the viewing area so that the entire element is on the screen. 

## Digitizer Audible Feedback 
Activates a voice describing the actions you are doing when making a digital model from your sheet model map. 

## Stop reporting warnings after: 
Provides an option to limit the list of warnings you want to identify when running an analysis. Preferring to list a lot of warnings can slow down your computer's performance.
modeling:
## Base Output Voltage 
Defines the preferred output voltage to be used by displays and printouts. 

## Single Phase Base kVA 
Defines the system-wide base kVA to be used with per unit based calculations. While this value will have no direct impact on results, extreme settings may increase round off errors. 100 kVA is recommended for distribution operating voltages. 

## Default Base kV 
Defines the system-wide default base kV. This value is only used as a default and has no impact on correctly defined systems. Set this field to the most commonly used nominal operating kV. 

## Earth Resistivity 
Gives the value (in ohm-meters) that will be used to model the earth’s resistivity. The default value for this field is "100" ohms. This value is used for calculation of overhead and underground line impedance. 

## System Frequency (hertz) 
Selects the cycles per second to specify the system frequency. This value should be “60” for 60 Hertz systems. 

## Lines with an angle measure of zero are understood to travel... 
Sets the reference direction from which the relative angle of a line is determined. Valid values are “North”, “South”, “East”, or “West”. 

## Center Tap Boundary Voltage 
Defines the preferred output of amperage desired. 

## OH Resistance Temp 
Allows you to select the temperature (25º or 50º Celsius) to determine which resistive value will be used in the calculation of the overhead impedance matrices. You must set the resistive value of each overhead and underground conductor using the Equipment Editor. 

## Transmission Threshold LG kV 
Any circuit elements whose L-G base kV is higher than the value set here will have a Circuit Level of Transmission. 

## Secondary Threshold LG kV 
Any circuit elements whose L-G base kV is lower than the value set here will have a Circuit Level of Secondary. 

Elements whose L-G base kV is between the transmission and secondary threshold values will have a Circuit Level of Primary. An element's Circuit Level may be viewed by adding the Circuit Level element field to a query in the Selected Elements Window. 

# System Default Construction Types
Selects the construction type definition to be used on all overhead and underground line elements with a blank or invalid construction type definition. 

We recommend that System Default Construction Type be set to the most commonly used construction type and that all line elements not built to this construction type be set to a blank construction type. This method will result in the most efficient method of data entry for construction type definition. 

*Tip: The “Modeling” tab under System Preferences has changed. There is no longer a System Default Construction Type field. Now there are four fields: Overhead, Overhead Secondary, Underground, and Underground Secondary.*

## Overhead 
Will be applied to new primary overhead lines whose kV is equal to or greater than the Secondary Threshold if no element-specific default has been defined under Circuit Element Preferences, and if their parent element does not have a construction type. This default will also be applied to imported overhead lines that have no construction type. If the user has not defined a construction type for these defaults, WindMil will attempt to find equipment named _defaultOHConst in the EQDB. 

## Overhead Secondary 
Will be applied to new primary overhead lines whose kV is less than the Secondary Threshold if no element-specific default has been defined under Circuit Element Preferences, and if their parent element does not have a construction type. This default will also be applied to imported overhead lines that have no construction type. If the user has not defined a construction type for these defaults, WindMil will attempt to find equipment named _defaultOHSecConst in the EQDB. 

## Underground 
Will be applied to new underground lines whose kV is equal to or greater than the Secondary Threshold if no element-specific default has been defined under Circuit Element Preferences, and if their parent element does not have a construction type. This default will also be applied to imported underground lines that have no construction type. If the user has not defined a construction type for these defaults, WindMil will attempt to find equipment named _defaultUGConst in the EQDB. 

## Underground Secondary 
Will be applied to new underground lines whose kV is less than the Secondary Threshold if no element-specific default has been defined under Circuit Element Preferences, and if their parent element does not have a construction type. This default will also be applied to imported underground lines that have no construction type. If the user has not defined a construction type for these defaults, WindMil will attempt to find equipment named _defaultUGSecConst in the EQDB. 

If an underground line has no defined construction type, and there is an overhead construction type, but there is no underground default construction type, the underground line will use the overhead default construction type during WindMil analysis routines.

## Load Location for new Circuit Elements 
In the past, there was not a WindMil feature that allowed a user to show a detailed model. The user would just place their load on a line element (for example, a consumer), knowing that there were hundreds of consumers. 

With the load location drop-down box, the user would preference WindMil to place the load at the source end (which is the upstream end of the line), uniformly spread it all over the line, or place the location at the end of the line (which is the downstream line end). 

## Load Mix Type 
Specifies the load mixes to use for all overhead, underground, node, and motor circuit elements that have a blank or invalid load mix specification. 

We recommend that the load mix for new circuit elements be left blank and that the load mix types be set to the most commonly-used load mix definition. This method will result in the most efficient method of data entry for load mix definition. 

*Tip: Hover over each Load Mix Type to see specific instructions for use.*
project_management:
## Enable Project Management 
Determines whether project management will be used to track model changes. When checked, project management is in use and the project management window is visible.

## Enable Dependency Autochecking 
Determines whether project management will keep track of which changes in a project depend on previous changes in other projects. When checked, project management will ensure that projects will apply their dependent projects before applying themselves.

## Save Operations For 
Allows users to choose which text-box data operations to track in project management, such as the movement of calculated data boxes, the visibility of labels, and the text of circuit element notes.

 - **Calculated Data Boxes:** When checked, project management will track whether calculated data boxes are visible and their X/Y coordinates on the model. 
 - **User-Definded Data Boxes:** When checked, project management will track whether user-defined data boxes are visible, the name of each template, and their X/Y coordinates on the model. 
 - **Notes:** When checked, project management will track whether circuit element notes are visible, the text of each note, the "Also Points To..." setting of each note, and their X/Y coordinates on the model. 
 - **Labels:** When checked, project management will track whether label X/Y coordinates on the model. Label visibility and status (whether the text is the element name or its map name) is always tracked by project management.
